Here’s a fast 2025 roundup of the biggest LLM/model moves (with dates)

- Jan 2025 — DeepSeek releases its open‑weights reasoning model R1, kicking off the “long‑thinking” model race. OpenAI follows weeks later by pushing new o‑series updates. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.12948?utm_source=openai))
- Feb 18 — xAI announces Grok 3 (new flagship chatbot/model). In Aug 2025, xAI open‑sources Grok 2.5. ([axios.com](https://www.axios.com/2025/02/18/elon-musk-grok-3-chatbot-openai?utm_source=openai))
- Feb 24 — Anthropic ships Claude 3.7 Sonnet (adds integrated advanced reasoning), later landing on AWS Bedrock in early March. ([axios.com](https://www.axios.com/2025/02/24/anthropic-claude-sonnet-reasoning?utm_source=openai))
- Feb 27 — OpenAI unveils GPT‑4.5 as a research preview. ([openai.com](https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-4-5/?utm_source=openai))
- Mar — Google DeepMind debuts Gemini 2.5 (focus on “thinking” improvements and an optional Deep Think mode tested later at I/O). ([blog.google](https://blog.google/technology/google-deepmind/gemini-model-thinking-updates-march-2025/?utm_source=openai))
- Mar 12 — Google launches Gemma 3 (open models, multimodal, long‑context). ([blog.google](https://blog.google/technology/developers/gemma-3/?utm_source=openai))
- Apr 8 — Amazon adds Nova Sonic (speech‑to‑speech model) to Bedrock; later expands Nova into the Nova 2 family by year‑end. ([press.aboutamazon.com](https://press.aboutamazon.com/2025/4/introducing-amazon-nova-sonic-a-new-gen-ai-model-for-building-voice-applications-and-agents?utm_source=openai))
- Apr 16 — OpenAI introduces o3 and o4‑mini (reasoning models), with o3‑pro rolling out in June. ([openai.com](https://openai.com/index/introducing-o3-and-o4-mini/?utm_source=openai))
- Apr–May — Microsoft releases Phi‑4 reasoning variants (small, open‑weights family tuned for structured reasoning). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.21318?utm_source=openai))
- May 22 — Anthropic launches Claude 4 (Opus 4 and Sonnet 4), a major step‑up for coding/agents; later in Nov adds Opus 4.5. ([anthropic.com](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-4?aad=BAhJIkJ7InR5cGUiOiJjb3Vyc2UiLCJ1cmwiOiJodHRwOi8vd3d3Lmluc2VhZC5lZHUiLCJpZCI6NjYxNjE3NzV9BjoGRVQ%3D--077f41e3bd1c4a6e4be9100a76319829a19f04ca&utm_source=openai))
- Nov 18 — Google rolls out Gemini 3 Pro; Dec 17 brings the fast, widely available Gemini 3 Flash. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Gemini?utm_source=openai))
- Dec — Mistral releases the Mistral 3 family, including Mistral Large 3 (open‑weights sparse MoE; 41B active/675B total params) and new “Ministral 3” small models. ([mistral.ai](https://mistral.ai/news/mistral-3?utm_source=openai))
- Dec 11 — OpenAI announces GPT‑5.2 (next GPT‑5‑series upgrade aimed at pro/agentic work). ([openai.com](https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-5-2?utm_source=openai))
- Also notable opens/long‑context: Qwen2.5 released 1M‑token open models (Jan 26 report) and later Qwen2.5‑Omni‑7B. Anthropic pushes 1M‑token context for Claude Sonnet 4. Amazon’s Nova 2 Sonic ships with a 1M‑token context window. ([qianwen-res.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com](https://qianwen-res.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/Qwen2.5-1M/Qwen2_5_1M_Technical_Report.pdf?file=Qwen2_5_1M_Technical_Report.pdf&utm_source=openai))

Key 2025 themes in one line
- Reasoning-first models went mainstream (OpenAI o‑series, DeepSeek R1, Microsoft Phi‑4 reasoning). Open/open‑weights had a renaissance at frontier scale (Mistral Large 3, Qwen2.5). Long context (up to 1M tokens) and agentic tool use spread across stacks (Claude 4, Nova 2, Gemini 3).

Want this broken down by use case (coding, agents, retrieval, on‑device) or a vendor‑by‑vendor capability matrix?

inputSnapshot.title: Bloom's Taxonomy & AI — 30 Second Manifesto
inputSnapshot.text:
For decades, education has been built on Bloom's Taxonomy — a pyramid of thinking, from simple recall at the base, to creation at the peak.

AI has just collapsed the bottom three levels.

Remembering. Understanding. Applying. AI does all of it — instantly, at scale, for free.

This changes everything. The classroom built around memorization is obsolete. The credential built around recall is worthless.

What remains irreducibly human sits at the top of the pyramid — analysis, judgment, creation.

The education system that survives the Second Renaissance will stop teaching the bottom of the pyramid and start building minds that live at the top.
